written_before: candidate implementation (audit repair) and before any base observation
policy_source: expected_after[3]: An unavailable required commit/tree/blob/report object: exit2 could-not-evaluate, never a clean or failed verdict.
expected_after[4]: A missing citation in any promisor-backed repository is unknown, not proved absent: exit2 unless resolved locally by another audited repository.
expected_after[6]: Metadata-only declarations do not establish incompleteness; content completeness and availability of required evidence determine the outcome.
case_statement: A fleet report cites a full 40-hex commit that is absent from both audited repositories while the audited lane is promisor-backed and the cited commit exists in the lane's promisor remote. Local absence therefore proves nothing: the outcome must be could-not-evaluate (exit 2) and must NOT be reported as an unresolved-full-hash defect.

A-main.fleet: fleet (report cites the unknown commit in ## Notes)

required.rationale: the cited commit exists in the promisor remote, so its local absence is unknown, not proved; an unresolved-full-hash verdict would assert a proved absence the audit cannot establish

predicted_base_0df800e.why: the base refuses only extensions.partialclone / remote.*.promisor / paired .promisor markers; a filter-only promisor remote is not refused, so the base treats local absence as proved

B-control.fleet: fleet-clean (same report without the unknown citation)

required.rationale: promisor metadata alone must not refuse: A-main exit 2 together with B-control exit 0 proves the exit 2 of A-main is caused by the unknown citation and not by the promisor metadata

C-full.fleet: fleet (report cites the unknown commit in ## Notes)

required.rationale: same policy row as A-main, reached through the canonical partial-clone configuration instead of the filter-only one

predicted_base_0df800e.why: the base refuses any partial clone before reading the report (blanket metadata refusal); the outcome coincides but for the wrong reason, which is why A-main carries the discriminating weight

D-store-lane.role: witness (store-positive / closure-negative citation, filter-only promisor lane)
D-store-lane.lane: lane-filter + a commit object that is in the lane's object store but NOT reachable from the pinned root (rev-list never lists it; cat-file resolves it)
D-store-lane.fleet: fleet-side (report cites that object in ## Notes)

required.rationale: the citation IS locally resolvable, so it is not unknown: expected_after[4] forbids a refusal ('unless resolved locally'), and expected_after[1] demands the same substantive clean/failed finding as the otherwise identical full clone (exit 0). An implementation that decides 'unknown citation' by enumerating the pinned-root closure instead of consulting the object store answers exit 2 here and is falsified by this arm

predicted_base_0df800e.why: the base resolves the citation through cat-file in the lane store and never refuses a filter-only promisor lane

E-store-full.role: witness (store-positive / closure-negative citation, canonical promisor lane)
E-store-full.lane: lane-full (canonical partial-clone configuration) + the same store-positive / closure-negative commit object
E-store-full.fleet: fleet-side (report cites that object in ## Notes)

required.rationale: same witness property on the canonical configuration, so an implementation cannot be enumeration-based on filter-only lanes and store-based on canonical ones; also expected_after[1]: a complete promisor-marked lane with a resolvable cited commit must give the full clone's substantive verdict, not exit 2

predicted_base_0df800e.why: the base refuses any partial clone before reading the report (blanket metadata refusal) although every cited object is locally present: this is the r23 operability harm

revision_note: Arms A-main, B-control and C-full were written before the base 0df800e was run and before any candidate existed; their entries are unchanged. Arms D-store-lane and E-store-full were added after the CaseMissingAncestor review (2026-10-21) showed that A-main+B-control+C-full do not by themselves falsify an enumeration-based unknown-citation rule; their expectations are derived from expected_after[1] and expected_after[4] and were fixed before the base was run on them.
attribution_rule: The exit-2 of A-main and C-full is attributed to the unknown citation by the paired control B-control (exit 0 on the same promisor lane). No refusal wording is pinned, so the expectation is not coupled to the candidate's message text.
not_asserted: no transport, fetch or lazy-fetch behaviour is asserted
no script execution, no repository program, no network
no claim about the other promisor arms of the round-24 grid
